items.title: How to answer a Telugu reading passage (పఠన అవగాహన పద్ధతి)
items.body:
## The task (అంశం 4)

A **~250-word Telugu prose passage (గద్యభాగం)** is given with **five short-answer questions** — **10 marks**. You are being tested on *understanding*, not memory, so **every answer must come from the passage**.

## A 4-step method

1. **మొదటి పఠనం (first read)** — read the whole passage once for the గిస్ట్ (overall sense). Do not stop at hard words yet.
2. **ప్రశ్నలు చదవడం (read the questions)** — now read the five questions so you know what to look for.
3. **రెండో పఠనం (second read)** — read again, **underlining** the sentence that answers each question.
4. **సమాధాన రచన (write answers)** — answer **to the point, in complete Telugu sentences**, in your own words where asked.

## Question types you will meet

| రకం (type) | English | ఏం చేయాలి |
|---|---|---|
| కేంద్ర భావం | Main idea | State the one theme of the whole passage |
| అంతరార్థం | Inference | Conclude what is implied, not stated |
| సందర్భానుసార పదార్థం | Vocabulary-in-context | Meaning that fits the sentence |
| ప్రత్యక్ష సమాచారం | Factual recall | Report the stated fact exactly as the passage gives it (e.g. the place or date named) — not from general knowledge |
| ధోరణి / ఉద్దేశం | Tone / purpose | Judge the writer's attitude/intent |

**Golden rule:** never add your own opinion or outside information, and never copy the whole passage.
keyPoints: Comprehension = ~250-word Telugu passage + 5 short-answers, 10 marks (item 4); answers come only from the passage.
Method: read for gist → read the questions → re-read and underline answers → write concise, complete-sentence answers.
కేంద్ర భావం (main idea) = the single theme every sentence supports.
అంతరార్థం (inference) = a conclusion the passage implies but does not state.
సందర్భానుసార పదార్థం (vocabulary-in-context) = the meaning that fits the sentence, not any dictionary sense.
Never add personal opinion or outside facts; never copy the whole passage.
items.mnemonic: Read–Question–Re-read–Reply (4 R's) for any comprehension passage.
items.source: standard Telugu comprehension method (SSC standard); APPSC 07/2026 Telugu item 4

items.title: Vemana Satakam — verse elaboration (వేమన శతకం)
items.body:
## About Vemana

**వేమన (Vemana)** was a people's poet whose **ఆటవెలది (Ataveladi)** verses teach **worldly ethics (నీతి)** in simple **spoken Telugu**. Every verse ends with the makutam **విశ్వదాభిరామ వినురవేమ** ('O Vema, hear this, delight of the world').

## Sample verse + elaboration

> అల్పుడెపుడు పలుకు నాడంబరముగాను
> సజ్జనుండు పలుకు చల్లగాను
> కంచు మ్రోగినట్లు కనకంబు మ్రోగునా
> విశ్వదాభిరామ వినురవేమ

**ప్రతిపదార్థం (word sense):** అల్పుడు = mean person; ఆడంబరముగా = pompously; సజ్జనుడు = noble person; చల్లగా = calmly/softly; కంచు = bronze; కనకంబు = gold; మ్రోగునా = does it ring?

**భావం (purport):** A mean person boasts loudly, while a noble person speaks gently. Just as **bronze rings loudly but gold does not**, showiness is not a mark of greatness — **quiet worth outshines noisy display**.

## How to elaborate (అంశం 2, ~100 words, 20 marks)

1. Open with the **theme** in one line.
2. Give the **bhavam** (not word-by-word).
3. Add a **real-life example** and a **closing moral**.

**Don't confuse:** **ప్రతిపదార్థం** = the meaning of each word, one by one (పదానికి పదం అర్థం); **భావం / తాత్పర్యం** = the purport of the whole verse in your own words. In an elaboration you expand the **భావం**; the ప్రతిపదార్థం is only a stepping stone. Counting syllables (అక్షరాలు) is metre analysis (ఛందస్సు), not elaboration.
keyPoints: Vemana wrote in the ఆటవెలది metre in simple spoken Telugu; makutam = విశ్వదాభిరామ వినురవేమ.
Verses teach నీతి (worldly ethics/morals).
Sample bhavam: bronze rings loud, gold does not — humility/quiet worth beats noisy show.
Elaboration (item 2) = expand the bhavam in ~100 words, any 2 of 3 verses, 20 marks.
Structure an elaboration: theme line → bhavam → example → moral.
Don't confuse: ప్రతిపదార్థం = word-by-word meaning; భావం/తాత్పర్యం = overall purport of the verse.
items.mnemonic: Vemana = 'Vinuravema' + Ataveladi; Sumati = 'Sumati' + Kanda — pair the makutam with the metre.

items.title: Sumati Satakam — verse elaboration (సుమతీ శతకం)
items.body:
## About the Sumati Satakam

The **సుమతీ శతకం**, attributed to **బద్దెన (Baddena / Bhadra Bhupala)**, is a set of **కందపద్యాలు (Kanda verses)** giving **practical moral counsel**. Every verse ends with the makutam **సుమతీ** ('O wise one').

## Sample verse + elaboration

> ఉపకారికి నుపకారము
> విపరీతము గాదు సేయ వివరింపంగా
> అపకారికి నుపకారము
> నెపమెన్నక సేయువాడు నేర్పరి సుమతీ

**ప్రతిపదార్థం:** ఉపకారి = one who helps; ఉపకారము = a good turn; అపకారి = one who harms; నెపమెన్నక = without counting faults; నేర్పరి = the skilled/wise one.

**భావం (purport):** Repaying a helper with help is nothing special. The **truly wise person does good even to one who has harmed him**, without dwelling on the wrong done. It praises **magnanimity** — returning good for evil.

## Exam tip

Name the **poet, metre and makutam** in your opening line, then give the **bhavam** and a modern example (e.g. forgiving an opponent). Keep it ~100 words.
keyPoints: Sumati Satakam is attributed to Baddena and written in the కందపద్యం metre; makutam = సుమతీ.
It gives practical nीति (moral counsel) for daily conduct.
Sample bhavam: the wise repay even harm with good, without counting faults — magnanimity.
Open an elaboration by naming poet + metre + makutam, then expand the bhavam with an example.
'సుమతీ' means 'O wise/good-minded one' — the poet addresses the reader.

items.title: Main idea, inference & tone — telling them apart
items.body:
## Three skills that trip up beginners

**1. కేంద్ర భావం (Main idea).** The **one theme** the whole passage supports. Test each option: *does every sentence relate to it?* A true main idea is broad enough to cover the passage but not so broad it covers unrelated things.

**2. అంతరార్థం (Inference).** A conclusion the passage **implies but does not state**. Ask: *what must be true given these lines?* Reject any option that (a) contradicts the passage or (b) adds outside information.

**3. ధోరణి / ఉద్దేశం (Tone / purpose).** The writer's **attitude/intent**, read from word choice:

| Signal words | Tone / purpose |
|---|---|
| దయచేసి…, తగ్గించండి (please…, reduce) | విజ్ఞప్తి / persuasive appeal |
| ముప్పు, జాగ్రత్త (danger, beware) | హెచ్చరిక / cautionary |
| అభినందనీయం, గొప్ప (praiseworthy) | ప్రశంస / appreciative |
| ఇది జరిగింది, ఇవి గణాంకాలు (this happened, data) | సమాచారాత్మక / informative |

**Discrimination tip:** the main idea is *what* the passage says; the tone is *how/why* the writer says it.
keyPoints: Main idea = the one theme every sentence supports; test options against the whole passage.
Inference = implied conclusion; reject options that contradict or add outside facts.
Tone/purpose = the writer's attitude/intent, read from signal words.
Persuasive appeal uses 'please/should'; cautionary uses 'danger/beware'; informative just states facts.
Main idea = WHAT the passage says; tone = HOW/WHY it is said.

items.title: Vocabulary-in-context & synonyms in comprehension
items.body:
## Meaning from context (సందర్భానుసార పదార్థం)

Many Telugu words have **more than one sense**; the passage decides which one applies. Use the **surrounding clues**:

- 'కరువు వచ్చి పంటలు ఎండాయి' → **కరువు = drought/famine — వర్షాభావం / దుర్భిక్షం** (not 'festival', not 'plenty').
- 'ఆయన మాట తీరు మధురం' → **తీరు = manner/style** (not 'shore').

**Method:** substitute each option into the sentence; keep the one that still makes sense.

## Handy synonyms (పర్యాయపదాలు)

| పదం | పర్యాయపదాలు (synonyms) | English |
|---|---|---|
| నీరు | జలం, ఉదకం, వారి, సలిలం | water |
| సూర్యుడు | రవి, భానుడు, ఆదిత్యుడు, భాస్కరుడు | sun |
| చెట్టు | వృక్షం, తరువు, మ్రాను, పాదపం | tree |
| ఇల్లు | గృహం, నివాసం, సదనం, గేహం | house |
| తల్లి | మాత, జనని, అమ్మ | mother |

Comprehension questions often ask a **synonym or the meaning** of a key word from the passage — knowing common pairs saves time.
keyPoints: Vocabulary-in-context: choose the sense that fits the sentence, using surrounding clues.
Method: substitute each option into the sentence and keep the one that makes sense.
నీరు = జలం/ఉదకం/వారి/సలిలం (water); సూర్యుడు = రవి/భానుడు/ఆదిత్యుడు (sun).
చెట్టు = వృక్షం/తరువు/మ్రాను (tree); ఇల్లు = గృహం/నివాసం/సదనం (house); తల్లి = మాత/జనని (mother).
Comprehension often asks a synonym/meaning of a passage word — learn common pairs.

items.title: Satakam basics and the famous satakams (శతకం — మకుటం, కవి)
items.body:
**In one line:** a **శతకం (satakam)** is a collection of about **100 verses** (often **108**) in which **every verse ends with the same signature word or line**, the **మకుటం (makutam)**.

**Why it is asked:** item 2 of the paper sets three verses from the **Vemana** and **Sumati** satakams and you elaborate any **two of three**, about 100 words each, for **20 marks**; naming the poet, metre and makutam in your first line shows you know the verse, and objective Telugu tests love *satakam → makutam* and *satakam → poet* pairs.

**What makes a satakam (శతక లక్షణాలు):**
1. **సంఖ్యా నియమం** — about 100 verses (often 108).
2. **మకుటం** — the same ending in every verse (the poet's "signature").
3. **One theme / mood** — నీతి (ethics), భక్తి (devotion) or వైరాగ్యం (detachment).

**Famous satakams — poet and makutam:**

| Satakam | Poet (కవి) | Makutam (మకుటం) | Metre |
|---|---|---|---|
| వేమన శతకం | వేమన (Vemana) | విశ్వదాభిరామ వినురవేమ | ఆటవెలది |
| సుమతీ శతకం | బద్దెన (Baddena) | సుమతీ | కందం |
| భాస్కర శతకం | మారన వెంకయ్య (Marana Venkayya) | భాస్కరా | ఉత్పలమాల / చంపకమాల |
| దాశరథీ శతకం | కంచర్ల గోపన్న (Bhakta Ramadasu) | దాశరథీ కరుణాపయోనిధీ | ఉత్పలమాల / చంపకమాల |
| నరసింహ శతకం | శేషప్ప కవి (Seshappa Kavi) | భూషణవికాస శ్రీధర్మపురనివాస | సీసం |

**About Vemana (వేమన):**
- Called **ప్రజాకవి (people's poet)** and **యోగి వేమన**; wrote in **simple spoken Telugu** against superstition, caste pride and hypocrisy.
- **C. P. Brown (Charles Philip Brown)** collected, printed and translated Vemana's verses into English, which made them widely known.
- **AP angle:** **Yogi Vemana University** is at **Kadapa** (YSR Kadapa district), Andhra Pradesh.
- Scholars **disagree on his date** — estimates range from the **14th to the 17th century**, so never state one year as settled.

**About Baddena (బద్దెన):** a 13th-century poet, also called **భద్రభూపాలుడు (Bhadra Bhupala)**; besides the Sumati Satakam he wrote **నీతిశాస్త్ర ముక్తావళి (Nitisastra Muktavali)**.

**Remember it:** *Vema → విశ్వదాభిరామ; Baddena → సుమతీ; Bhaskara → భాస్కరా; Ramadasu → దాశరథీ.*

**Don't confuse:** **సుమతీ** is the makutam of Baddena's satakam, not a poet's name; **వేమ** alone is not the full makutam — it is **విశ్వదాభిరామ వినురవేమ**.
keyPoints: A satakam = about 100 verses (often 108), each ending in the same makutam (మకుటం).
వేమన శతకం — Vemana — makutam విశ్వదాభిరామ వినురవేమ — ఆటవెలది metre.
సుమతీ శతకం — Baddena (Bhadra Bhupala, 13th century) — makutam సుమతీ — కందం metre.
భాస్కర శతకం — మారన వెంకయ్య — makutam భాస్కరా; దాశరథీ శతకం — కంచర్ల గోపన్న (Ramadasu) — makutam దాశరథీ కరుణాపయోనిధీ.
నరసింహ శతకం — శేషప్ప కవి; Baddena also wrote నీతిశాస్త్ర ముక్తావళి.
C. P. Brown collected, printed and translated Vemana's verses; Yogi Vemana University is at Kadapa (AP).
Vemana = ప్రజాకవి writing in spoken Telugu; his date is disputed (14th to 17th century).

items.title: The two metres you will meet — ఆటవెలది and కందం
items.body:
**In one line:** Vemana's verses are in **ఆటవెలది (Ataveladi)** and Baddena's are in **కందం (Kandam)**; knowing their shape helps you read the verse line by line before you elaborate it.

**Why it is asked:** metre is the first thing you name in an elaboration opening, and metre rules are a favourite objective question.

**Key terms first:**
- **పాదం (padam)** = one line of a verse. Both metres have **4 పాదాలు**.
- **గణం (ganam)** = a fixed group of syllables; **గురువు (U)** = heavy/long syllable, **లఘువు (I)** = light/short syllable.
- **సూర్య గణాలు** = **న (III)** and **హ / గల (UI)**.
- **ఇంద్ర గణాలు** = **భ, ర, త, నల, నగ, సల**.
- **యతి** = the agreement of the first letter of a line with a letter at a fixed later place; **ప్రాస** = the same second letter in every line.

**ఆటవెలది (Vemana):**

| Line | Ganas |
|---|---|
| Odd lines (1 and 3) | 3 సూర్య గణాలు + 2 ఇంద్ర గణాలు |
| Even lines (2 and 4) | 5 సూర్య గణాలు |

- Yati falls on the **first letter of the 4th gana**; **ప్రాస నియమం లేదు** (no prasa rule).

**కందం (Baddena):**

| Line | Ganas |
|---|---|
| Odd lines (1 and 3) | 3 ganas |
| Even lines (2 and 4) | 5 ganas |

- Ganas allowed: **గగ, భ, జ, స, నల** (each worth 4 మాత్రలు).
- **ప్రాస is compulsory**; an **odd-place gana must not be జ**; the **6th gana must be జ or నల**; the **last syllable is a గురువు**.

**Remember it:** *Ataveladi = no prasa, Surya + Indra; Kanda = prasa compulsory, 3 + 5 ganas.*

**Don't confuse:** ఆటవెలది and తేటగీతి both mix Surya and Indra ganas, but only ఆటవెలది has **five Surya ganas in its even lines**.
keyPoints: పాదం = one line; both ఆటవెలది and కందం have 4 పాదాలు.
సూర్య గణాలు = న (III) and హ/గల (UI); ఇంద్ర గణాలు = భ, ర, త, నల, నగ, సల.
ఆటవెలది: odd lines 3 సూర్య + 2 ఇంద్ర గణాలు; even lines 5 సూర్య గణాలు.
ఆటవెలది: yati at the first letter of the 4th gana; no prasa rule (ప్రాస నియమం లేదు).
కందం: odd lines 3 ganas, even lines 5 ganas; ganas గగ, భ, జ, స, నల.
కందం: ప్రాస compulsory; odd-place gana not జ; 6th gana జ or నల; last syllable guru.

items.title: Question words, title and scoring the 10 marks (ప్రశ్నార్థక పదాలు)
items.body:
**In one line:** the five short questions on the **~250-word passage** use Telugu question words; each answer must give exactly the kind of information the question word asks for.

**Why it is asked:** a correct fact written for the wrong question word ("when" answered with a place) scores nothing.

| Question word | Asks for | Answer begins with |
|---|---|---|
| ఎవరు (evaru) | who — a person | the person's name |
| ఏమి (emi) | what — a thing or action | the thing/action |
| ఎప్పుడు (eppudu) | when — a time | the time/date |
| ఎక్కడ (ekkada) | where — a place | the place |
| ఎందుకు (enduku) | why — a reason | కాబట్టి / వల్ల (because) |
| ఎలా (ela) | how — a manner | the way it is done |

**How to do it (exam steps):**
1. Read the passage once for the gist, then read the five questions.
2. Underline the line that answers each question.
3. Write each answer as **one or two complete Telugu sentences** — 10 marks for 5 answers means about **2 marks per answer**.
4. If a **శీర్షిక (title)** is asked, give a short phrase naming the central idea.

**Factual recall (ప్రత్యక్ష సమాచారం):** for who/when/where questions the answer is stated directly in one line — copy the fact, not the whole line.

**Paper rules that decide the result:** the Telugu paper is **qualifying** — marks are **not counted for merit** — but you must reach **40% (OC/EWS/Sports)**, **35% (BC)** or **30% (SC/ST/PBD)**.

**Remember it:** *question word → answer type; one fact per answer, in a full sentence.*
keyPoints: ఎవరు = who; ఏమి = what; ఎప్పుడు = when; ఎక్కడ = where; ఎందుకు = why; ఎలా = how.
Five short answers for 10 marks = about 2 marks per answer; answer in full Telugu sentences.
శీర్షిక = title: a short phrase naming the central idea.
Telugu paper is qualifying — not counted for merit; minimum 40% OC/EWS/Sports, 35% BC, 30% SC/ST/PBD.
items.source: APPSC Notification 07/2026 — Telugu (Qualifying) items 2 & 4; SSC-standard Telugu (శతక సాహిత్యం, ఛందస్సు)
